summary: The video side is a raster-driven pipeline. Everything is timed off hcnt/vcnt: an 8-pixel character fetch, a background address built by adder chains on the flipped H/V counters, and a per-line sprite search into a 32-entry online RAM followed by an hblank fetch into a line buffer. That is the board's structure, not MAME's per-frame draw_background/draw_sprites batch. Two parts follow MAME, though. The sprite DMA copies MAME's guessed congo_sprite_custom_w loop step for step. The sound board's analog drum/gorilla circuits are replaced by a WAV sample player triggered on exactly the PPI port bits MAME's samples handlers use. Overall the core leans hardware, with MAME-derived pieces where MAME was the only reference.

findings.signal: raster counters drive every fetch phase
findings.note: The character layer reads video/color RAM at hcnt(2:0)="010". Its address is vflip(7:3)&hflip(7:3), and it shifts the ROM bits out pixel by pixel. That is a scan-time tile fetch, not MAME's tilemap abstraction.

findings.signal: background as adder chain on flipped H/V
findings.note: map_offset_h/l1/l2 are combinational sums of bg_position, vflip and hflip2 that feed the map and graphics ROM addresses every pixel. MAME instead indexes a pre-rendered bg pixmap row by row. The arithmetic agrees, but the core puts it in the address path the way the board's adders do.

During the active line, sprite RAM is scanned at sprite RAM rate. Entries whose Y sum has the top 3 bits = "111" go into sp_online_ram. In hblank they are fetched at fixed hcnt(3:0) slots and written into a line buffer, which is cleared as it is read out. MAME instead loops over offs 0x7c..0 and searches for a minimum Y/X per frame.

A buffer write happens only when the existing pixel is "000", which gives first-written-wins priority inside the line buffer. That falls out of the hardware structure, while MAME expresses it as transpen draw order.

Work, char and sprite RAM addresses are muxed between CPU/DMA and the video scanner by hcnt(0), like a board sharing the RAM bus by pixel-clock phase. MAME has no such contention. Partly an FPGA convenience.

Coin inputs are edge-latched flip-flops held clear by the coin enable bit. The IRQ is a flip-flop set on the vblank edge and held clear while int_on=0. Semantically this matches MAME, but it is written as registered logic rather than callbacks.

The step machine triggers on a write of 0x01 to C033. It reads the first byte as daddr*4 (dma_do(5:0)&"00"), copies 4 bytes, advances the source by +28 at step 4 for a 0x20 stride in total, and runs count+1 times (stops when dma_cnt=0). This is the same algorithm MAME's loop uses, a loop MAME's own code treats as a guess about the custom chip.

The analog drum and gorilla circuits are replaced by 5 WAV files stored with their RIFF headers, played at 11.025 kHz. Each starts on a falling edge of port_c bits 0-3 or port_b bit 1, the same bits and channels MAME's samples handlers use. Gorilla only starts when it is not already playing, which matches MAME's !playing(0) check.

findings.signal: sound IRQ from counter reset on INTACK
findings.note: The sound IRQ is bit 10 of a divider chain that is cleared by IORQ during interrupt acknowledge. That is how a counter-based board circuit behaves; MAME uses a periodic irq_hold instead. PSG READY lines drive WAIT_n.
The masks (E03B/E038/E03F) reproduce the same mirrors as congo_map (0x1fc4, 0x1fc7, 0x1fc0). A correct core and emulator must both have them.
Char beats sprite beats background, chosen per pixel by building the palette address. This is the same order as MAME's bg/sprites/fg draw sequence, but resolved at scan time.
